newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INJURED CONTE MUST WAIT TO KNOW HIS FATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURED CONTE MUST WAIT TO KNOW HIS FATE.

text.p: Midfielder Antonio Conte could be out of soccer for up to six months after injuring his knee in Italy's 1-0 World Cup qualifying win over Georgia.

European Cup holders Juventus said on Thursday initial checks showed he had strained cruciate ligaments in his left knee but heavy swelling and fluid meant more detailed tests would have to be postponed.
The 27-year-old club captain, certain to miss his side's European Champions' League tie at Rapid Vienna next Wednesday, will have more tests in 10 days.
If they show he has torn cruciate ligaments, Conte will need surgery that would put him out of action for around six months.
"We hope it is not that serious," a Juventus spokesman said.
Conte twisted his knee in the second half of Wednesday's game and had to be substituted.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi said he was not unduly troubled by the prospect of losing a key player.
"We have a large and competitive pool," he said. "At the start of the next intensive period, with seven games in 21 days, I would have had to bring in fresh players anyway.
"This will be yet another chance to show how strong we are. There are no seasons without setbacks."
